title: Janus_Tachyon_Star
purpose: Bridge the long-running JANUS TACHYON causal-anchor research line, the forensic POSS-I/Palomar transient program, and the newly recovered one-exposure LUCI1 near-infrared point-source candidate at a frozen Palomar source coordinate. The artifact records the observation without erasing prior negative controls, and treats TACHYON STAR as a named falsifiable physical hypothesis rather than as a conclusion promoted by nomenclature alone.

historical_tachyon_program_boundary.previous_epistemic_boundary: The earlier JANUS TACHYON artifact used TACHYON as project language for memory, temporal anchors, causal graphs, and future-consequence modeling and explicitly did not claim experimentally confirmed tachyons or physical transmission into the past.
historical_tachyon_program_boundary.effect_of_current_artifact: The LUCI observation adds an independent astronomical candidate layer to the TACHYON research line. It does not retroactively rewrite the earlier symbolic/software status into a proven particle claim.

jpfm_2e_result.forensic_interpretation: In the dense S0 cohort the original ANY_CANDIDATE association is exactly the Palomar observing-schedule association, not evidence that nuclear-window dates generated more photographic candidates.

palomar_forensic_boundary.nonnuclear_baseline: POSS-I transient candidates are documented outside nuclear-test windows; therefore nuclear testing is not a necessary generator condition for the catalogued class.
palomar_forensic_boundary.registry_rule: A nuclear or other external-event trigger may remain a falsifiable modulator hypothesis only if it survives observation-opportunity, weather, geomagnetic, lunar, plate, morphology, and independent-instrument controls.

new_observation.observation_interpretation: A marginal R1-compatible PSF-like point-source candidate was measured close to the frozen Palomar coordinate in a single LUCI1 Br_gamma exposure. Its width is nearly identical to the frame-native PSF, but the signal is weak and the preregistered matched-control morphology requirement is not satisfied.

luci_population_context.reason: The all-42 negative result was not achieved because one source remains sensitivity-unresolved and a different source produced one counterpart candidate.

janus_tachyon_star_hypothesis.name: TACHYON_STAR_TRANSIENT_HYPOTHESIS
janus_tachyon_star_hypothesis.author_interpretation: Hawkar/JANUS working interpretation: the historical Palomar star-like transient line and the newly observed short-lived near-IR point-source event may belong to a physical transient class provisionally named JANUS TACHYON STAR.
janus_tachyon_star_hypothesis.minimal_testable_form: At least some Palomar-coordinate events correspond to real, short-lived sky-origin point-source phenomena whose temporal behavior cannot be explained by static celestial counterparts and that survive detector, plate, moving-object, atmosphere, astrometry, and statistical-noise controls.
janus_tachyon_star_hypothesis.strong_physical_form: The surviving class is associated with tachyonic or superluminal physics.

nuclear_trigger_subhypothesis.statement: Specific high-energy external events, including nuclear detonations, may modulate the observability or production rate of the proposed transient class.
nuclear_trigger_subhypothesis.reason: JPFM-2E showed the original binary nuclear-window association was exactly confounded with Palomar observing opportunity in the dense S0 cohort, while the wider POSS-I literature and JANUS audit contain a non-nuclear baseline.

alternative_explanations_that_remain_liv: detector defect or transient bad-pixel behavior
cosmic-ray or particle interaction with the detector
ordinary astronomical transient or variable source
chance alignment with a field source

required_tests: forced photometry at the exact frozen sky coordinate across the complete same-night LUCI1 Br_gamma sequence
difference-image residual analysis using immediately preceding and following sensitivity-qualified frames
per-pixel detector-coordinate tracking across dithers to separate sky-fixed from detector-fixed behavior
bad-pixel, persistence, saturation, nonlinearity, cosmic-ray and readout diagnostics
PSF-fit likelihood comparison against empirical local stars with a preregistered adequate control count
moving-object ephemeris and apparent-motion exclusion for the observation time and sky position
independent remeasurement by a second implementation blinded to the candidate frame identity
search for independent contemporaneous astronomical coverage when available
predefined decision table distinguishing SKY_TRANSIENT, MOVING_OBJECT, DETECTOR_EVENT, NOISE, and UNRESOLVED
falsification_and_adjudication_gate.promotion_rule: TACHYON_STAR may be promoted from project hypothesis to a new observational class only after a sky-origin transient survives the mundane-control gate. Promotion to tachyonic physics additionally requires an independent observable capable of discriminating tachyonic/superluminal physics from ordinary transient astrophysics; transient duration alone is insufficient.
falsification_and_adjudication_gate.failure_rule: If detector-fixed, noise, moving-object, atmospheric, or ordinary astrophysical explanations account for the event under the preregistered gate, preserve this artifact as a negative/redirect certificate rather than deleting or rewriting it.

FACT: JANUS has a pre-existing TACHYON causal-anchor research line whose v1.0 core explicitly did not claim verified physical tachyons or physical time travel.

The JPFM-2E dense S0 analysis found that ANY_CANDIDATE was identical to Palomar observation-night membership, making the original OR=1.409 binary association a schedule association rather than candidate-frequency evidence.
LUCI-PALOMAR JPFM-2F-F preserved 92 parent qualified negatives and raised source-level sensitivity-qualified no-counterpart coverage from 39/42 to 41/42.

One LUCI1 Br_gamma frame contains a pipeline-defined marginal point-source candidate near the frozen coordinate, bracketed by qualified no-counterpart frames 232.6 seconds before and 432.3 seconds after.
INTERPRETATION: The one-frame behavior is compatible with a short-lived event but is not sufficient to establish sky origin.
The near equality between candidate FWHM and native PSF makes the event worthy of targeted adjudication but does not override its low SNR or insufficient matched-control count.
OPEN_HYPOTHESIS: A real short-lived physical sky-source class connects at least a subset of the Palomar transient line with the LUCI one-frame event.
JANUS TACHYON STAR is an appropriate provisional name for that class while the physical mechanism remains under test.
A high-energy external-event modulation may exist after opportunity and environmental controls, but no nuclear causal effect is currently admitted.
NOT_ADMITTED: The LUCI candidate is a confirmed counterpart of the historical Palomar photographic event.
The LUCI candidate proves the existence of a tachyon.
The Palomar transient population consists of tachyons.
Nuclear detonations create, attract, reveal, or photograph tachyons.
The candidate demonstrates superluminal propagation, retrocausality, time travel, artificial origin, UAP origin, ETI origin, or a common cause across the Palomar population.

canonical_statement: JANUS TACHYON STAR is now a registered observational hypothesis anchored to a concrete LUCI1 one-exposure PSF-like candidate at a frozen Palomar coordinate. The observation is real as a pipeline candidate; its sky origin and tachyonic identity remain open questions to be decided by the 2F-G adjudication gate, not by the name of the artifact.
append_only_rule: Do not delete or silently rewrite this v1.0 artifact if the hypothesis fails. Future evidence must be appended as a new version, adjudication result, or negative certificate with explicit lineage.

safety_and_scope.nuclear_context: Historical/event-correlation analysis only. No weapon design, construction, acquisition, optimization, targeting, or operational instructions are in scope.
safety_and_scope.scientific_scope: Astronomical transient adjudication, provenance, causal inference, falsification, and reproducibility.
